text: Treating rice straw with urea increases its nutritive value: urea (commonly sold as fertilizer) is mixed with water and applied to straw; naturally occurring microorganisms in the straw break down the urea, releasing ammonia, which dissolves tough fiber (making the straw more digestible) and raises its nitrogen content (supporting rumen microbe growth) — treated cattle eat more straw as a result. Key production factors: use 5 kg of urea per 100 kg of dried rice straw; mix 1 kg of urea into 10 liters of water; ferment for 2 weeks in the dry season (above 30°C) or 3 weeks in the rainy season (cooler, slower fermentation); seal the straw airtight throughout fermentation. Consumption/planning: a 300 kg animal can eat about 6 kg/day, so 2 cattle need about 12 kg/day; for a 3-week fermentation cycle, prepare 12 kg × 21 days = 252 kg per batch; 100 kg of treated straw takes up about 1 m³, so the storage silo should be more than 2.5 m³. Using two silos of about 3 m³ each lets the farmer feed from one while the next batch ferments in the other, alternating continuously.
